memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make for the tent a covering of ram skins dyed red, and over that a covering of the other durable leather." - Exodus 26:14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Two more layers went over the tabernacle: ram skins dyed red, and above them a covering of tough, weather-resistant leather. Four layers in all now — beauty on the inside, strength on the outside. The layer that faced the sun, the sand, and the storms was the plainest and toughest of all.

From the outside, the tabernacle would not have looked impressive. A traveller passing by would see only weathered leather. All the glory — the gold, the colours, the woven cherubim — was on the inside, visible only to those who entered. God's dwelling was far more beautiful within than it appeared without.

Isaiah would later write of the Messiah that He had no beauty or majesty to attract us, nothing in His appearance to draw us to Him (Isa 53:2). Jesus came looking ordinary, a carpenter's son from an unremarkable town. The glory was there, but you had to come close to see it. And this is often how God works still — His greatest treasures are not displayed on the surface. Paul says we hold this treasure in jars of clay, so that the surpassing power belongs to God (2 Cor 4:7). Do not judge by outward appearance, whether of others or of yourself.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I judge people, or myself, too quickly by outward appearance?
Do I believe God can hold real treasure in an ordinary-looking life?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You place great treasure in plain vessels. Keep me from judging by appearances, and thank You that Your glory can dwell in an ordinary life like mine. Amen.
